posts.text:
Italy got a king in 1861, but not a finished country. Rome and Venice were still missing from the map. A thread on the unfinished kingdom.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ On 17 March 1861, Victor Emmanuel II, king of Sardinia, was proclaimed King of Italy. The Kingdom of Sardinia had absorbed most of the peninsula, including Sicily and the south.
2/ Look closely at the map: the Papal States shrink to a small patch around Rome, and the northeast (Venetia) is still inside the Habsburg Empire. Italy exists, but with two big holes.
3/ Venetia joined in 1866, after Italy fought alongside Prussia against Austria. A plebiscite there backed annexation almost unanimously, though historians note it was held under military pressure.
4/ Rome came next. Italian troops captured it in 1870, and it became the capital in 1871. Before that the capital had been Turin, then Florence.

5/ So 1861 is the start of the process, not the end. The unification itself took from 1848 to 1871, depending on where you draw the line. Which date would you pick? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
